20 Some illnesses that can affect driving
20.1 Respiratory allergies
Tips for drivers with allergies:
Not drive with the windows open. The air will contain large quantities of pollen, so it will increase the allergic reaction.
Do not put the air conditioning on strongly. The direct jets of air will cause an allergic reaction.

questions.help:
Road traffic collisions
 
3 Characteristics of road collisions
Related studies that have investigated traffic collisions, show that:
In cities, the accidents that cause the most mortalities are collisions with pedestrians.
Most of the victims, especially resulting in deaths, occur on intercity routes.
Most collisions occur on the straight and not on bends.
Autopistas and autovias are generally safer than conventional roads.
Most accidents occur during public holidays (especially, Easter, summer and December).
Weekends and public festivals (bank holidays) are the most dangerous days, especially during the hours in the morning.
Most accidents occur during the daytime when people are going to or leaving work, especially at the end of the working day.
(Página 250 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Check the tyre pressures using a properly approved and tested tyre gauge at least once or twice a month. These can be found at public and private locations.

Active safety is also called primary safety as it is any activity whose purpose is to prevent an accident, acting before it occurs and including preventive measures such as control of the tyres, brakes, etc.

The purpose of the suspension system is to ensure that the wheels are in constant contact with the road surface, thus providing maximum road adherence and stability and ensuring passenger comfort by preventing the irregularities of the road being felt by the occupants. (Página 244 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
Safe driving  
 
8 Driving in fog
Fog is very dangerous as, not only does it reduce visibility but the adhesion quality (grip) is also lowered, as the road surface becomes wet.
Therefore, when driving in fog it is necessary to:
Use lights: the front dipped headlights or / and the front fog light (if fitted) together with the position lights and, in the case of thick fog, the rear fog light(s).
It is not recommended to use the main beam headlights as the fog reflects back the vehicles own lights (the water drops act like a mirror) and cases dazzle to the driver.
Keep the cabin well ventilated to avoid the windows misting up.
Adapt the speed to the visibility and view of the road ahead.
 
(Página 232 del manual 'Learning to drive')

ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS    
 
17 Influence of drugs in road traffic collisions
Not only alcohol seriously alters the ability to drive a vehicle.
Some pharmaceuticals and the majority of drugs also affect driving because they cause intoxication, problems with attention and concentration and a decreased reaction ability in drivers. If they are mixed with alcohol, the risk of accident is much greater, as it strengthens many of the side effects of these products, and can even produce totally unpredictable reactions.
(Página 43 del manual 'Learning to drive')

OTHER FACTORS
 
24 Food
A large meal, which is not easily digested can cause drowsiness and increase driver fatigue. Conversely, if little food is consumed or the period between meals is too long dizziness may occur, which will adversely affect the driver.
The advice is to eat light meals or several snacks and to wait some time after a main meal before driving.
It is advisable to drink a lot, although you may not feel thirsty, in order to ensure proper hydration and thereby reduce the potential for increased fatigue and sleepiness.
The drinking of water or juices is recommended and of course, alcoholic beverages must not be drunk.
(Página 50 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Road traffic collisions
 
13 Transferring casualties
Always, whenever possible, await the arrival of an ambulance with persons and doctors adequately trained. Only in exceptional cases should you transfer casualties to the nearest hospital. For example:
In an isolated area with no chance of asking for and receiving assistance.
If the help is delayed for over 30 minutes and the casualty presents a progressive state of unconsciousness with symptoms of shock or a severe haemorrhage, that continues to bleed profusely and can’ be stemmed or it has been necessary to place a tourniquet on the casualty
(Página 267 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Road traffic collisions
 
13 Transferring casualties
Any transfer of the casualty should be done using a lorry or van, so you can place them in an adequate position and at the same time it is possible to have a person next to them to carry out resuscitation if necessary and calm the victim.
During the transfer the driving should be soft, at an adequate speed for the state of the road and volume of traffic so as not to aggravate the injuries.
(Página 267 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
4 Position lights
 
4.4 Usage in immobilizations
Any vehicle stopped or parked between sunset and sunrise, either on any road or on the hard shoulder of an in town highway – which is insufficiently illuminated, must display position lights. However under these circumstances it is possible to replace the position lights with parking lights. Two position lights or two parking lights must be illuminated and these must correspond to the side of the vehicle closest to the road.
(Página 99 del manual 'Learning to drive')

7 ‘U’ turn    
7.3 Circumstances when it is prohibited to undertake a ‘U’ turn
It is specifically prohibited to carry out a ‘U’ turn:
At level crossings (although it is not prohibited in their immediate surroundings).
In tunnels, underpasses and sections of the road affected by the signal “unnel”.
On motorways and dual carriageways, except in the places designated for this purpose.
On one-way roads and one-way sections of roads.
In general, in all sections of the road where overtaking is prohibited, unless a ‘’turn is expressly authorized.
(Página 195 del manual 'Learning to drive')
